quest.title: The Arrival of the Sabzeruz Festival
quest.description: As agreed, you go to the festival with Dunyarzad and others... Wait... This feels somewhat familiar...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Mora x22775, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: This is divine wisdom...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Oh! We're gonna be late. It's all because you wouldn't get out of bed!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should go meet Dunyarzad right away!

talks.objective: Go to the appointed place and talk to Dunyarzad

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good morning, Dunyarzad! Sorry we're late, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Not at all. I arrived early.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... You seem kinda tired... Did you not get enough sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I'm doing well. There's no need to worry. Shall we go? Let's start with the stalls over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure... Uh? Traveler, why are you just standing there? Let's get going!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: This is a stall offering foods from the Haft-Mewa Feast.

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: You are quite well-informed, Miss! I thought most people nowadays wouldn't know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're all plants... Aw, Paimon's a little disappointed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, what is the "Haft-Mewa Feast" you mentioned just now?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It's one of the Sabzeruz Festival's traditions. People used to set their tables with seven different foods to symbolize the seven virtues of the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: ...The remnants appear to be in the form of the Moon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Paimon thought it looked like some kind of food.

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: Hmm... The Moon signifies... Hmm... It's escaping me for now. Wait a moment...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is he really looking it up in a book?

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: Oh, right, it means illusions and lies.

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: But if you trust your intuition and overcome your fears, the sun will surely rise.

choices.text: I feel like I've heard this before...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Understood. I'll keep that in mind.

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: Oh, it's nothing. I'm just learning as I go, haha... ha...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess that was still pretty interesting. Okay, on to the next stall.

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: I picked all of these from the forest yesterday, so their freshness is guaranteed!

dialogues.speaker: Children
dialogues.text: Farris! Farris!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Alright soldiers, now that you have your Yalda Candies, don't forget your loyalty to Lesser Lord Kusanali. Dismissed!

dialogues.speaker: Children
dialogues.text: Yes, Knight Farris!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on? Is this a play?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Farris, the Knight of Flowers, is another Sabzeruz Festival icon, and one immensely popular with children.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Haha, it's all thanks to Miss Dunyarzad's sponsorship that the children can meet the Knight of Flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Oh, do you want some Yalda Candies? I happen to have some boxes readied here. Take a look and pick whichever one you want.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, what's to pick? Don't these boxes all look the same?

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Haha, it's not that simple. Each box contains a random flavor — it's up to the luck of the draw. Flavors include Lavender Melon, Harra Fruit, Sunsettia...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, how interesting!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: ...And there's also Lizard Tail and Onikabuto.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh! Why do those flavors even exist!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Traveler, help Paimon pick one. Paimon wants to eat the Sunsettia flavor!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Great. These boxes of candy are numbered one to five from left to right. Which one do you want?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number one.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Ah, excellently chosen! Number four is indeed Sunsettia.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha, Paimon bet you had incredible luck, and Paimon was right!

choices.text: Just now... Did I really mean to choose number four?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Are you saying that you instinctively chose the right box?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, but now that you mention it... Paimon also had the feeling you'd choose the right one... Is that kinda like what you felt?

choices.text: Why do I keep having this sense of déjà vu...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe we didn't sleep very well last night, or maybe we slept too much.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm sorry, Dunyarzad, but I need to leave for a moment.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Oh, sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Where are you going? You're just gonna walk off like that?

choices.text: It felt like... my body just subconsciously reached for it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number two.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number three.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number four.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Ah, excellently chosen! Number four is indeed Sunsettia.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha, Paimon bet you had incredible luck, and Paimon was right!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That just now... I don't think that was luck.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't know why, but I knew it must have been number four.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? How's that possible? It's obviously random...

choices.text: Why do I keep having this sense of déjà vu...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number five.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A feeling of... déjà vu?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows what that is! It's when you feel like you've already experienced whatever is going on...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, Paimon also felt something like that today... But that's just our brains playing tricks on us, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, why'd you run here in such a hurry?

choices.text: I want to do something I normally never would.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's it! You're intentionally doing things you usually wouldn't, and seeing if you still get that same feeling of déjà vu...

response.speaker: Lambad
response.text: Welcome, you two! Are you here for lunch? What would you like to eat?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: One Charcoal-Baked Ajilenakh Cake, please.

response.speaker: Lambad
response.text: Got it. You don't look like you're from these parts, but I gotta say, you've got good taste. I'll give this order to the kitchen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Charcoal-Baked Ajilenakh Cake! Isn't it that... that burned thing that didn't look tasty at all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Paimon understands what you're trying to do now... You'd never normally order something like this...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some time, the Charcoal-Baked Ajilenakh Cake is served...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That... thing... Are you really gonna eat it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't this... going a bit too far...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Here goes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—How was it? The look on your face is telling Paimon that it tasted awful...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No... It actually tasted really good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, you mean...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's impossible! We were just talking about how gross it looked...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So would this be a case of taste bud déjà vu?

choices.text: I couldn't get rid of it after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon also gets the impression that we've been here many times, even though we aren't regulars.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm... How about... we go out again and try something else.

choices.text: Looks like I tried this before.
I want to see if I can get rid of this déjà vu.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Dunyarzad is sitting by herself on that bench over there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a coincidence, Dunyarzad! We meet again! Uh, why are you sitting here all by yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh, I ran into some kidnappers just now, but thankfully, Dehya came to my rescue. I started to feel unwell after that, so I sat down here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kidnappers? Oh my goodness! Are you hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I'm okay. Dehya's arm got scratched, but it isn't serious.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... That's a big relief. But Dunyarzad, you seem a little down today... It's the Sabzeruz Festival, and you've been looking forward to it so much.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Not at all. I've always been like this. Excessive physical exertion or strong emotions tend to aggravate my illness.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Besides, no matter how amazing today may be, it is but a single day. After however many more days, my time will come to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't quite follow you, and Paimon feels like something's really got you down right now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry for leaving you behind earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It really is fine. I don't mind.

choices.text: I just experienced a number of strange events...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Huh? Did something happen?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dunyarzad... have you ever felt déjà vu? You know... Like when you've already experienced something that's happening right now?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Déjà vu? No, but my days have been the same for years now. Even if I were feeling déjà vu, I suppose I would already be used to it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon sees... Then, is it only the two of us...?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It's almost time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Time for what?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Nilou's Dance of Sabzeruz is about to begin. Let's go.

choices.text: Have you noticed anything out of the ordinary?

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Bazaar and see the Dance of Sabzeruz

dialogues.speaker: Azar
dialogues.text: ...With your lack of intellectual credentials, I do not believe you are qualified to debate with me. What you should be doing is finding workers to tear down this ridiculous eyesore.

dialogues.speaker: Azar
dialogues.text: When we return, have the Scribe draft an ordinance before the next Jnagarbha Day that prohibits public art performances. We will announce it to the public later via the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Understood. I will inform him when I return.

dialogues.speaker: Azar
dialogues.text: The Sabzeruz Festival... Go celebrate the birth of that god to your heart's content.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, Dunyarzad, the Grand Sage ordered us to stop the performance...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It's okay. There's nothing we can do about it.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: But you've been really looking forward to this. I don't want you to have any regrets...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It truly is unfortunate, but I don't wanna cause trouble for anyone. Didn't the Grand Sage say that he might investigate the organizers?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: True, but... *sigh* Well, okay, we'll just have to try again next year, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: The next festival... I probably won't be around by then.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Wait... What did you just say?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: No, nothing. I'll be heading back to rest. Thank you for your help, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe what those heartless geezers did!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did Dunyarzad already go back? We should also return and get some sleep.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The Sabzeruz Festival was forced to come to an unfortunately abrupt end...

choices.text: For some reason, I felt like this outcome was inevitable.

talks.objective: Return to the accommodation and rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So in the end, you still couldn't figure out what that déjà vu feeling was all about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe it really was because of exhaustion...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Same here! That's why Paimon stopped thinking about it halfway through the day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then how about we settle in and get a good night's sleep. For now, we can chalk things up to exhaustion... We can do more thinking tomorrow!
*beep*
...Observing a modest drop in the output of Jnana Energy, but values still remain within normal parameters.
Continue to monitor for variances in the data, and find the cause as soon as possible.

choices.text: I hadn't thought about it, but my head does feel very heavy.

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* How am I supposed to conduct business when I'm not allowed to leave the city?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Atten-tion! Any more requests, young soldiers?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, they're selling food over that way! Let's go take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... where to next?
